name: James Alfred Van Allen
summary: American space scientist who discovered Earth's radiation belts and contributed to the development of the proximity fuse.

name: Thomas Poulter
summary: Physicist and mentor to James Van Allen at Iowa Wesleyan College.

name: Abigail Halsey
summary: Wife of James Van Allen.

name: George Ludwig
summary: Graduate student and research assistant to James Van Allen.

name: Carl McIlwain
summary: Research assistant to James Van Allen.

name: Sydney Chapman
summary: Geophysicist and DTM research associate who advised Van Allen.

name: Lloyd V. Berkner
summary: Geophysicist who proposed the International Geophysical Year.

name: Nicholas Constantine Christofilos
summary: Physicist at Lawrence Berkeley Lab who proposed detonating bombs in space.

name: Bernard Lovell
summary: British radio astronomer who protested nuclear testing in space.

name: Iowa Wesleyan College
summary: College where James Van Allen studied physics as an undergraduate.

name: Carnegie Institution of Washington's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism
summary: Research institution where Van Allen completed a postdoctoral fellowship.

name: State University of Iowa
summary: University where Van Allen earned his graduate degrees and later chaired the physics department.

name: Applied Physics Laboratory
summary: Laboratory managed by Johns Hopkins University where Van Allen worked during and after WWII.

name: U.S. Naval Reserve
summary: Military branch in which Van Allen was commissioned during World War II.

name: Jet Propulsion Laboratory
summary: Laboratory that built and operated the Explorer satellites.

name: Army Ballistic Missile Agency
summary: Agency that launched the Juno 1 missile carrying Explorer 1.

name: Mount Pleasant, Iowa
summary: Birthplace and hometown of James Van Allen.

name: Cape Canaveral
summary: Launch site for the Bumper V-2 and later space missions.

name: Johnston Island
summary: Location of high-altitude nuclear tests including Starfish Prime.

name: South Atlantic Ocean
summary: Location of the Project Argus nuclear tests.

name: Hawaii
summary: Location where effects of the Starfish Prime test were observed.

name: Soviet Union
summary: Country Van Allen visited in 1959 and competed with in the space race.

name: V-2 rocket
summary: German rocket used for high-altitude research after World War II.

name: Explorer 1
summary: First U.S. satellite which carried Van Allen's instrument package.

name: Explorer 4
summary: Satellite purpose-built to monitor the Project Argus nuclear tests.

name: Van Allen Belts
summary: Zones of energetic charged particles surrounding Earth discovered by Van Allen.

name: Project Argus
summary: Top secret military test to detonate atomic bombs in space.

name: Project Starfish Prime
summary: 1962 high-altitude nuclear test that created an artificial radiation belt.

name: radio-proximity fuse
summary: Device designed by Van Allen during World War II to detonate bombs near targets.
